## Summary: Design Tokens & CSS Custom Properties Patterns

Based on my exploration of the kynetic-spec-ui web-ui package, here's how design tokens and CSS custom properties are used for colors:

### 1. **Design System Token Foundation** 
Located at: `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/src/lib/ds/tokens.css`

The project uses a comprehensive design token system with **CSS custom properties** defined in OKLCH color space:

- **16 Core color tokens**: `--design-bg`, `--design-fg`, `--design-card`, `--design-primary`, `--design-secondary`, `--design-muted`, `--design-accent`, `--design-destructive`, `--design-border`, `--design-input`, `--design-ring`, etc.
- **7 Status colors with foreground pairs**: 
  ```css
  --design-status-pending
  --design-status-pending-fg
  --design-status-in-progress
  --design-status-in-progress-fg
  --design-status-pending-review
  --design-status-pending-review-fg
  --design-status-needs-work
  --design-status-needs-work-fg
  --design-status-completed
  --design-status-completed-fg
  --design-status-blocked
  --design-status-blocked-fg
  --design-status-cancelled
  --design-status-cancelled-fg
  ```
- **4 Severity colors** (error, warning, info, success) with muted and border variants
- **7 Spacing, 4 radius, 7 z-index, 3 font tokens**
- Dark mode support via `.dark` class selector with adjusted OKLCH values

### 2. **Tailwind v4 Theme Integration**
Located at: `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/src/app.css` (lines 78-201)

The `@theme` block maps CSS custom properties to Tailwind color utilities:

```css
@theme inline {
  --color-status-pending: var(--design-status-pending);
  --color-status-pending-fg: var(--design-status-pending-fg);
  --color-status-in-progress: var(--design-status-in-progress);
  /* ... etc */
}
```

This enables **Tailwind class usage** like `bg-status-pending` and `text-status-pending-fg` instead of raw colors.

### 3. **Existing Semantic Color Pattern Examples**

#### Status Colors (Recommended Pattern)
Found in multiple components (`TaskList.svelte`, `ItemDetail.svelte`, `TaskCard.svelte`):

```typescript
function getStatusColor(status: string): string {
  const colors: Record<string, string> = {
    pending: 'bg-status-pending text-status-pending-fg',
    in_progress: 'bg-status-in-progress text-status-in-progress-fg',
    pending_review: 'bg-status-pending-review text-status-pending-review-fg',
    needs_work: 'bg-status-needs-work text-status-needs-work-fg',
    blocked: 'bg-status-blocked text-status-blocked-fg',
    completed: 'bg-status-completed text-status-completed-fg',
    cancelled: 'bg-status-cancelled text-status-cancelled-fg'
  };
  return colors[status] || 'bg-status-cancelled text-status-cancelled-fg';
}
```

**Note:** There's also a **centralized utility** in `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/board/board-utils.ts` (lines 21-60):

```typescript
export function getStatusClasses(status: string): { bg: string; fg: string; label: string } {
  const map: Record<string, { bg: string; fg: string; label: string }> = {
    pending: { bg: 'bg-status-pending', fg: 'text-status-pending-fg', label: 'Pending' },
    // ... etc
  };
  return map[status] || { bg: 'bg-muted', fg: 'text-muted-foreground', label: status };
}
```

This is **imported and used** in TaskCard.svelte (line 9) and should be the model for new color utilities.

#### Step Type Colors (Current Issue)
Found in `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/src/routes/workflows/+page.svelte` (lines 31-36):

```typescript

  action: 'text-emerald-500',      // ❌ Raw Tailwind color

  decision: 'text-amber-500'       // ❌ Raw Tailwind color
};
```

**This is the pattern you need to replace.** It uses raw Tailwind colors instead of design tokens.

### 4. **Severity Colors Available (Not Yet Widely Used)**
```css
--design-severity-error      /* with -fg, -muted, -muted-fg, -border variants */
--design-severity-warning    /* with -fg, -muted, -muted-fg, -border variants */
--design-severity-info       /* with -fg, -muted, -muted-fg, -border variants */
--design-severity-success    /* with -fg, -muted, -muted-fg, -border variants */
```

These map to Tailwind as `bg-severity-error`, `text-severity-error`, etc.

### 5. **Priority Colors Pattern**
Found in `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/TaskList.svelte` (lines 60-65):

```typescript
function getPriorityColor(priority: number): string {
  if (priority === 1) return 'text-red-600 font-bold';      // ❌ Semi-semantic
  if (priority === 2) return 'text-orange-600 font-semibold';
  if (priority === 3) return 'text-yellow-600';
  return 'text-gray-600';

This uses semantic naming but could be improved with design tokens if needed.

export function getStepTypeClasses(stepType: string): { text: string; label: string } {
  const map: Record<string, { text: string; label: string }> = {
    action: { text: 'text-status-completed', label: 'Action' },      // or use a semantic token

}
```

- `action` → `text-severity-success` (positive action)
- `check` → `text-severity-info` (informational)
- `decision` → `text-severity-warning` (decision point)
